channel.title: The London Free Press - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The London Free Press (lfpress.com)

item.title: Transport truck driver flees scene of crash on Hwy. 401 at London: OPP
item.description: One person was injured in a crash on Highway 401 at London involving a transport truck that left the scene, Ontario Provincial Police say.

item.title: Builders react to London mayor's home ownership incentive push
item.description: New housing ownership incentive program would see city hall pick up 60 per cent of the tab for development charges on new builds.

item.title: Woodstock truck stop gets new lease on life
item.description: A Quebec-based company plans to reopen the former TA Truck Stop this spring.

item.title: London studies show promise for fecal transplants in cancer immunotherapy
item.description: Small clinical trials in kidney, lung and skin cancers suggest improved responses and fewer treatment side effects.

item.title: Using puppets, group aims to teach kids about fetal alcohol syndrome
item.description: Four renowned Canadian puppeteers are in London this week shooting a video series aimed at raising awareness about FASD.

item.title: With homeless shelter set to open, some nearby businesses beef up security
item.description: “We don’t know what to expect, so I guess it’s plan for the worst, hope for the best."

item.title: LHSC highlights new two-in-one surgery for complex aortic disease
item.description: The approach could reduce recovery time for patients, a surgeon says.

item.title: Free Press photographer Derek Ruttan leaves 'remarkable legacy'
item.description: Derek Ruttan, who died Monday, chronicled London's good, bad and ordinary for The Free Press for 28 years

item.title: Four South Asian teens injured in 'racist assault' at Victoria Park
item.description: The labour council said the attack was targeted, but police have not yet determined the nature of the incident.

item.title: London-area police opt out of federal gun buyback program
item.description: Police forces say they will remain focused on illegal firearms and violent offenders instead.
